This document outlines the maintenance procedures P1, which must be performed on 
yearly bases as indicated by Y1 in the title block.

The DL400, is a pilot wire relay for the protection 
of overhead lines and cables. the protection detects phase faults in unearthed 
systems and phase and earth faults in solidly or resistance earthed systems. the 
zone of protection may also include a power transformer.

The 
document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility of error causing 
personal injury or damage to equipment.

Rabee, accepted by general manager eng. Hamdy Dorgam of Damanhour power station and
certified by eng. Gaber 
farahat WDEPC inspection head sector and MPIS coordinator.

sections.text:
Return Relay and Associated Equipment to 
Service

items:
Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the relay terminal 
 block and the test set i.e.
 - Disconnect the test leads of the current terminals.
 - Disconnect the test leads between the trip contact.
Make sure CT secondary circuits are in normal condition.

If any equipment associated with the relay has been isolated, it should be 
 returned to service by the following restoration steps:
 - Breaker trip coils.
 - Breaker failure scheme associated this relay.
 - Disturbance alarm and fault recorder associated with this relay.

Introduction
This document outlines the maintenance procedures P1, which must be performed on 
yearly bases as indicated by Y1 in the title block.
The DL400, is a pilot wire relay for the protection 
of overhead lines and cables. the protection detects phase faults in unearthed 
systems and phase and earth faults in solidly or resistance earthed systems. the 
zone of protection may also include a power transformer.
The 
document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility of error causing 
personal injury or damage to equipment.
The first draft initiated by eng. Ahmad Galal, tested by eng. Mohamed 
Rabee, accepted by general manager eng. Hamdy Dorgam of Damanhour power station and
certified by eng. Gaber 
farahat WDEPC inspection head sector and MPIS coordinator.
Safety Precautions

Work to be Carried Out
Relays Preparation
Look at field maintenance file and compare the setting on relay with those 
 shown on the test sheet.
Set the earth link on the relay to line side position.
Test Steps
O/C terminal
Connect test leads between the current terminals ( 3 6) for phase ( R ).
Increase the current slowly until the relay operates.
Record this value in the test sheet.
Connect test leads between the current terminals ( 4 6) for phase S and 
 repeat the previous steps.
Connect test leads between the current terminals ( 5 6) for phase T and 
 repeat the previous steps.
For testing the time repeat the previous steps of the time.
Connect test leads between the current terminals ( 3 6) for phase R and 
 repeat the previous steps.
Disconnect the terminal 9 is (+VDC)
Connect test leads between the time terminals ( 9 10) for phase and 
 repeat the previous steps for phase S & phase T.
87PW Terminal
Connect the test leads between the current terminals ( 1 2 ).
Increase the current slowly until the relay operates.
Record this value in the test sheet.
Return Relay and Associated Equipment to 
Service
Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the relay terminal 
 block and the test set i.e.
 - Disconnect the test leads of the current terminals.
 - Disconnect the test leads between the trip contact.
Make sure CT secondary circuits are in normal condition.
If any equipment associated with the relay has been isolated, it should be 
 returned to service by the following restoration steps:
 - Breaker trip coils.
 - Breaker failure scheme associated this relay.
 - Disturbance alarm and fault recorder associated with this relay.
